clue.text: Potter's seven points get veto

definitions.meaning: in snooker, a potter sinks balls, and the black one is worth seven points
to reject or bar someone, as by a negative vote in a club ballot

explanation.surface: A ceramicist's score of seven earns a veto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' suggests a maker of pots, but here it is a snooker player, who pots balls; the black is the top-value ball at seven points.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude a candidate from a club was done by dropping a dark ball in the ballot box, so it means to reject.

clue.text: Jump one sees in fleapit

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the word fleapit, so 'in' points to a run tucked within it

explanation.surface: A jump you might see in a seedy old cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: A fleapit is British slang for a shabby, run-down cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to spring or bound is to jump.

clue.text: Group of friends sets firm time to go on the lake

indicators.note: the last piece is attached after the others, going on the end

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
Erie is one of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A circle of friends arranges a firm time for an outing on the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A close circle or clique of people sharing interests is a set of friends.

clue.text: The shortest way to buzz off?

definitions.text: The shortest way to buzz off?

parts.words: The shortest way to buzz off?
parts.note: a buzzing insect heading off by the most direct route gives a phrase for the straightest line between two points

explanation.surface: Asks for the quickest route for someone told to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz off' reads as a rude dismissal, but literally it is a bee flying away, and bees are said to fly straight home.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a direct straight-line route, named after the path a bee supposedly takes.

clue.text: Put down, face up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the face of a clock or watch is its dial

explanation.surface: Placed on the table with its front showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face up' looks like part of the definition, describing how something was laid down, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: placed or set down is the past form of lay.

clue.text: Rambling Lord I silenced-that was rash

indicators.note: rambling speech wanders about, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peer falls silent after a meandering speech, admitting that it was rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling' shuffles the thirteen letters of LORD I SILENCED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done hastily without proper thought is rash.

clue.text: Kith and kin Shylock couldn't separate?

definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice, Shylock may take a pound of flesh but no blood, which he cannot do

explanation.surface: Family that the moneylender of Venice couldn't pull apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Shylock is told his bond allows flesh but not one drop of blood, so the two cannot be parted.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for one's own relatives, and literally the two things Shylock could not cut apart.

clue.text: Ancient, and conveying impression of natural eminence?

definitions.meaning: resembling raised landforms in the countryside, read literally

explanation.surface: Something very old that also gives the look of a lofty landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom meaning extremely old; read literally it means looking like high ground.

clue.text: Travel in this out of this world

definitions.text: Travel in this out of this world

parts.words: Travel in this out of this world
parts.note: 'out of this world' sounds like praise, but here it means literally beyond Earth, a vehicle for such travel

explanation.surface: Recommends a wonderful way to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a craft that carries people beyond Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Strange embargo on this weapon

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the following words are made odd and rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd ban imposed on this particular weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges the letters of EMBARGO ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Australian curved throwing stick, a hunting weapon that returns.

clue.text: Speed of a quiet one

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: The speed of a calm individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rate of movement or tempo.

clue.text: Artist in attempt to arrange hair

indicators.note: the artist's letters go inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
RA is Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter tries to style someone's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To plait strands of hair together is to style it this way.

clue.text: Solo turn is capital

indicators.note: a turn here means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A solo performance counts as a big deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Able to leave wretched skinflint

indicators.note: the letters of able depart from the longer word

parts.note: miserable means wretched
the word able taken as written

explanation.surface: Being competent is a way to leave a wretched penny-pincher.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stingy person who hoards money.

clue.text: Boy in association is a spy

definitions.meaning: a boy belonging to the youth movement founded by Baden-Powell

explanation.surface: A member of a youth group turns out to be a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the youth organisation, and someone sent out to gather information.

clue.text: Lock up criminal-wonderful!

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
fine can mean excellent or wonderful

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims with delight that a criminal is being locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to imprison or shut in.

clue.text: Shout out old demand

parts.note: ex means former, old
a claim is a demand

explanation.surface: Someone yells an old demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cry out suddenly.

clue.text: Clergyman may spend it freely

indicators.note: used freely, the letters of the words before are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vicar is allowed to spend his pay as he likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges SPEND IT; the whole clue also describes the vicar's salary.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed salary paid to a clergyman, which he can spend.

clue.text: Send mad notes over the mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue the notes are placed above the mountains

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: Musical notes floating over the peaks drive someone crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make insane or disturb the mind.

clue.text: Firm's originator is to capsize

definitions.meaning: the person who establishes a company
to fill with water and sink

explanation.surface: The company's founder is about to capsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who establishes something, and also a verb for a ship sinking.

clue.text: Quite a long distance driver aims to reach

definitions.meaning: a golfer hitting with a driver aims at the mown strip between tee and green

explanation.surface: A motorist sets off on a long trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase for a considerable distance, and the closely mown part of a golf hole.

clue.text: Thought one nearly dead

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: nearly means stopping just short, losing the final letter

explanation.surface: A thought that someone is close to death.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a notion or concept.

clue.text: Annual cycle, or a little part

parts.note: taken as written
a bit is a small part

explanation.surface: Asks whether something is a yearly cycle or a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth's yearly circuit around the Sun.

clue.text: One gets omitted from simple scheme

indicators.note: the one is left out of the word meaning simple

parts.note: plain means simple
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person gets left out of a basic scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a proposed arrangement or design.

clue.text: Tips down? Barely a shower

indicators.note: written downwards in reverse, so the word tips is read backwards

explanation.surface: Advice about rain: hardly a shower at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A few drops of rain is described as a light spit.

clue.text: Indistinctly mouth aspersion

definitions.meaning: to pronounce words in a blurred way

explanation.surface: Mumbling an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak words run together, and also an insulting remark.

clue.text: Even in summer its leaves may be on the ground

definitions.text: Even in summer its leaves may be on the ground

parts.words: Even in summer its leaves may be on the ground
parts.note: a tree whose drooping branches hang so low that its foliage touches the earth all year, not just in autumn

explanation.surface: A tree whose foliage reaches the ground in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: a tree with long hanging branches that trail to the ground.

clue.text: Ready? Let's move, finding our balance

indicators.note: move signals the letters shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ready to go, someone urges departure in order to recover equilibrium.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of weighing scale with a beam and a sliding weight.
